{{Quote|On Nagi, there are things we find beautiful... we prize things for their strength... or their workmanship... or their elegance.|[[Den Siva]]|<ref name="marvel97">[[Star Wars (1977) 97|''Star Wars'' (1977) 97]]</ref>}}
'''Nagi''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in a [[Unidentified star cluster|star cluster]] of the [[Firefist]] satellite [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] that was gravitational [[Orbit/Legends|bound]] to [[The galaxy/Legends|the host galaxy]] and was part of the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]. Nagi was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Nagai/Legends|Nagai]] [[Species/Legends|species]], who built great cities of crystal and wire among the planet's expansive wastelands. The [[Tof/Legends|Tofs]] conquered Nagi in a long and bloody campaign starting around [[296 BBY]], and many Nagai would later leave Nagi in an [[Nagai–Tof War|attempt to wage war]] on the [[Alliance of Free Planets]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].

==Description==
Nagi was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]],<ref name="LECG" /> located in a dense [[Star cluster/Legends|star cluster]] at the edge<ref name="TEA" /> of the dwarf [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] known as [[Firefist]] that orbited the [[The galaxy/Legends|known galaxy]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Even by [[130 ABY]], few non-Nagai knew the world's location.<ref name="LECG" /> It was one of five planets in its solar system,<ref name="Gamer 1">{{GamerCite|1|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Marvel Series}}</ref> and had a single [[Moon/Legends|moon]]. Days on Nagi were 23 local hours long and years were 299 local days&mdash;the planet was 11,000 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] in diameter.<ref name="TEA" />

Nagi was an arid world, and quite mountainous, characterized by very high mountain peaks separated by deep, wide valleys. The thin upper atmosphere was relatively ineffective at blocking solar [[Radiation/Legends|radiation]], and the high peaks of the world were bathed in it. As a result, the deep valleys, which were often cast in shadow by the towering mountains, were the site of the Nagai's cities.<ref name="LECG" /> Nagi's sprawling wastelands were often wracked by ferocious storms that could cause vegetation to suddenly emerge in hours.<ref name="TEA" /> At the height of their civilization just prior to the [[Tof/Legends|Tof]] invasion, Nagai cities were composed of wire and crystal, and were perceived as beautiful.<ref name="Gamer 1" />

==History==
Nagi was the ancestral homeworld of the [[Nagai/Legends|Nagai]]. Around [[296 BBY]], the Nagai were reaching the height of their civilization, and were beginning to experiment with rudimentary [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] technology. An unmanned probe sent to explore the other planets of their star system, however, was detected by a Tof warship. The Tofs found Nagi an easy target for their depredations and immediately set about conquering the planet and enslaving the Nagai. The Nagai fought back, however, and unlike previous victims of the Tofs, survived not only the initial attack<ref name="Gamer 1 />&mdash;the invasion of Nagi cost the Tofs millions of casualties&mdash;<ref name="unk">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref> but also three hundred years of Tof oppression.<ref name="Gamer 1" />

[[File:Nagi_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Nagi]]
Enough Nagai evaded the Tofs to devote their remaining resources to defense and space travel, sending scouts into the galaxy to find targets for their own conquest. Finding the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]] at war, the Nagai scout [[Krai H'voc]] advised waiting until the defeat of the Empire before advancing on the rest of the galaxy. The Nagai allied with an Imperial splinter group under the command of [[Lumiya]] and fought on many worlds before Tof pursuers forced the Nagai into a peace agreement with the [[Alliance of Free Planets]], successor of the Rebellion. They defeated the invading Tof forces at Saijo, and while some Nagai chose to remain in the greater galaxy, the [[Nagai expeditionary force]], along with [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|Mandalore]] [[Fenn Shysa]] and his contingent of [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] resistance fighters, returned to Nagi to fight the Tofs still holding their homeworld.<ref name="Gamer 1" /> 

The arrival of the Nagai on the galactic stage led to considerable confusion about Nagi's location&mdash;the Nagai's claim that their homeworld was beyond the galactic rim was commonly disbelieved.<ref name="TEGAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> The Nagai and Mandalorians were successful in freeing the world, but the remnants of the Tof invasion remained visible across the globe as late as 130 ABY.<ref name="LECG" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Main|Nagai/Legends}}
The Nagai were [[near-Human]]s,<ref name="Gamer 1 note 1">{{GamerCite|1|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Marvel Series}}; the interbreeding of [[Krai H'voc]] with a [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] to produce a son, [[Bey]], indicates common biological ancestry.</ref> with pale skin, black hair, dark eyes, and slim builds. They were driven by their belief in personal honor, and feared only the loss of their freedom. They had little regard for those not of their family, though they would aid others if it served their purposes or their sense of honor. Their native language was [[Nagaian]].<ref name="LECG" /> Nagi had a total population of around 48 million, about eight percent of which were non-Nagai&mdash;the natives created beautiful cities of wire and crystal clustered around oases in the massive Nagi wastelands.<ref name="TEA" /> 

==Behind the scenes==
Nagi was first mentioned in [[Star Wars (1977) 97|''Star Wars'' (1977) 97]], written by [[Mary Jo Duffy]] and released in [[1985]].<ref name="marvel97" />
